Pin Language

Three views of the same object: the sweep the pin just flew (one room, seven gate poses), the sixteen words the pin speaks (each basis dimension decoded to its movement), and a flight annotated with what the pin said at every replan.

the whole sweep, one room

drag to orbit · wheel to zoom · shift-drag to pan

All seven extreme poses at once — each color is one gate pose (bright rectangle) with its five flights. The background cloud shows the gate at its ORIGINAL pose; each rectangle is where it actually stood for that cell. Toggle poses to unclutter.

the 16-word vocabulary (eigen-movements)

drag to orbit · wheel to zoom · shift-drag to pan

Type-specimen sheet, no room: each curve is one basis dimension decoded to the movement it commands (U e_k, denormalized, integrated; shape-normalized to ~0.9 m — true 2-sigma sizes are 5-35 cm). Rows are channels (x red, y green, z blue, yaw amber), columns are horizons, short to long left to right. Short-horizon words move then hold; long-horizon words keep moving through the whole chunk; yaw words curl because heading rotates the ongoing motion. Every command the pin ever carries is a weighted sentence of these sixteen.

what the pin said, replan by replan (behind-start flight)

drag to orbit · wheel to zoom · shift-drag to pan

Magenta curves: the served command decoded back into its coarse movement at each replan anchor — the literal content of the noise. The green flight is what the flow made of it. Where magenta and green agree in shape but green is richer, you are seeing the factorization: coarse from the pin, residual from the model.
